title: 6 Best Concrete Driveway Paints in 2026: Prep Decides Lifespan
h1: The 6 Best Concrete Driveway Paints in 2026
description: Behr Premium 1-Part Epoxy is the best concrete driveway paint of 6 picks; KILZ is the value choice. Asphalt needs a black sealer instead, not paint.
dek: Behr Premium 1-Part Epoxy is the best concrete driveway paint of 6 picks; KILZ is the value choice.
intro: The best concrete driveway paint for most homeowners is Behr Premium 1-Part Epoxy, a one-can epoxy-acrylic that the label rates for exterior concrete and vehicle traffic; KILZ 1-Part Epoxy Acrylic does the same job for less. If your driveway is asphalt, do not paint it at all: a black filler sealer such as Rust-Oleum EpoxyShield Blacktop is the right refresh.

Most painted driveways fail for the same few reasons: a product not made for tires and weather, skipped prep, or paint over concrete that was still pushing moisture up from below. Get those right and a coating can look sharp for several years. Get them wrong and it peels in the tire paths by the first winter. Below are six picks, then whether to paint, stain or seal, how to prep, apply and choose a color, and how long it lasts.
quickAnswer: For a concrete driveway, buy a one-part epoxy-acrylic paint rated for exterior use and vehicle traffic: Behr Premium 1-Part Epoxy overall, KILZ 1-Part Epoxy Acrylic for value, Seal-Krete Epoxy-Seal for low odor. Use Behr Porch and Patio only on walks and borders. For asphalt, use a black filler sealer such as Rust-Oleum EpoxyShield Blacktop or Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000 instead of paint. Prep, especially degreasing, etching and a moisture test, decides how long any of them lasts.

blocks.p: Paint is for concrete; asphalt gets sealer. On concrete, a one-part epoxy-acrylic paint is the sweet spot between durability and DIY ease: tougher than porch paint, far easier than a two-part epoxy system. On asphalt, a black filler sealer restores the look and protects the pavement, which is what most people asking about painting blacktop actually want.

sections.h: The 6 Best Concrete Driveway Paints in 2026, Ranked

blocks.p: Picks are ranked on what each maker states about surfaces, exterior use, vehicle traffic and cure times, plus recurring themes in owner reports. The first four are concrete paints; the last two are the right coatings for asphalt, which should not be painted.

blocks.h3: Best Overall for Concrete: Behr Premium 1-Part Epoxy Concrete and Garage Floor Paint

blocks.p: Behr's 1-Part Epoxy is an acrylic paint modified with epoxy ester, which gives it better grip and abrasion resistance than a porch paint while keeping the convenience of opening a can and rolling. There is nothing to mix and no pot life to beat. It is marketed for garage floors and other concrete that sees vehicles, with resistance to hot-tire pickup, and the label lists both interior and exterior concrete, which matters on a driveway exposed to sun and rain. It tints to a wide range of colors, so you can match trim or pick a gray that hides dirt. The catch is prep: like every floor coating, it needs clean, profiled concrete, which means degreasing and etching or grinding, and several days of cure before you park on it. Owners commonly report good results on well-prepared slabs and peeling where prep was skipped.
**Pros:** Single component, no mixing; marketed for hot-tire resistance; wide tint range; interior and exterior use per label; soap-and-water cleanup.
**Cons:** Not as hard as a true two-part epoxy; needs etching or grinding to bond; several days before cars.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Behr+Premium+1-Part+Epoxy+Concrete+Garage+Floor+Paint&tag=sktiger-20)

blocks.h3: Best Value: KILZ 1-Part Epoxy Acrylic Concrete and Garage Floor Paint

blocks.p: KILZ follows the same idea as the Behr pick: an acrylic with epoxy modifiers for extra toughness, sold as one component so you just open and roll. It is designed for concrete floors including areas with vehicle traffic, and the label lists exterior use as well as garages. Where it stands out is cost: it typically sells for less per gallon than comparable products, which adds up on a two- or three-car driveway that needs two coats. The color range is narrower, focused on practical grays and tans, which suits most driveways since a neutral tone hides tire marks and dirt. Rough, porous broom-finished concrete soaks up more paint than a smooth slab, so expect coverage at the low end of the label's range on an older driveway. The bond still depends on cleaning, degreasing and etching, so budget for those supplies too.
**Pros:** Usually priced below comparable 1-part epoxies; roll-on application; made for vehicle areas; water cleanup.
**Cons:** Fewer colors than Behr; coverage drops on rough concrete; same strict prep.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=KILZ+1-Part+Epoxy+Acrylic+Concrete+Garage+Floor+Paint&tag=sktiger-20)

blocks.h3: Best Low-Odor Option: Seal-Krete Epoxy-Seal Concrete and Garage Floor Paint

blocks.p: Seal-Krete Epoxy-Seal is another one-part, epoxy-modified concrete paint, set apart mainly by its low-VOC, water-based formula. Less odor while you work is handy when the driveway runs right up to an attached garage or the front door. It is intended for interior and exterior concrete and tints to a range of colors. Like the other one-part products, it bonds best to clean, etched concrete and goes on with a roller in two thin coats. Seal-Krete also makes cleaners, etchers and clear sealers, and some owners like using one brand for the whole sequence so the instructions line up. It is less universally stocked than Behr or KILZ, so you may need to order it. On a sloped drive, add an anti-slip aggregate to the last coat, since a smooth painted surface can be slick when wet.
**Pros:** Low-VOC, water-based; one component; tintable; interior and exterior concrete; low odor near the house.
**Cons:** Harder to find in stores; needs anti-slip grit on slopes; careful prep like any coating.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Seal-Krete+Epoxy-Seal+Concrete+Garage+Floor+Paint&tag=sktiger-20)

blocks.h3: Best for Walks, Borders and Aprons: Behr Premium Porch and Patio Floor Paint, Low-Lustre

blocks.p: Behr's Porch and Patio Floor Paint is a tough acrylic enamel for concrete and wood floors that see foot traffic, with one of the widest color selections around. On a driveway it has a specific job: the walkway that leads from the drive, decorative borders and bands, and areas beside the drive that see feet rather than tires. It is not formulated for repeated vehicle traffic the way the epoxy-modified paints are, and in tire paths it tends to scuff, lift or show hot-tire marks sooner. Many owners combine the two: a vehicle-rated paint on the driving lanes and this product in a matching or contrasting color on walks and edges. The low-luster finish hides small surface flaws better than gloss. Add an anti-slip additive on steps and sloped walks. Our [best porch paint](/best-porch-paint/) guide covers more options.
**Pros:** Huge range of tintable colors; low-luster finish hides flaws; easy roll-on; water cleanup.
**Cons:** Not built for tire paths; can be slippery when wet without grit; shorter life than epoxy-modified paint on a driveway.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Behr+Premium+Porch+and+Patio+Floor+Paint+Low-Lustre&tag=sktiger-20)

blocks.h3: Best for Asphalt Driveways: Rust-Oleum EpoxyShield Blacktop Filler and Sealer

blocks.p: Ordinary paint does not belong on asphalt. Its film cannot flex with the pavement, and oils in the asphalt can bleed through and soften it. The right way to refresh blacktop is a coating made for it, and Rust-Oleum's EpoxyShield Blacktop Filler and Sealer is a widely sold option. Despite the EpoxyShield name, it is a water-based asphalt coating, not an epoxy. Its fillers help close fine cracks and surface voids as it seals, leaving an even, deep black. You apply it with a squeegee or broom like any driveway sealer, and it follows the same weather rules: warm, dry conditions above the label minimum and no rain for the stated time. It does not replace a dedicated crack filler for anything wider than fine cracks. If you think you want to paint an asphalt driveway, this kind of product is almost always what you actually need.
**Pros:** Made for asphalt; fills fine cracks as it seals; restores an even black; squeegee or broom application.
**Cons:** Black only; wider cracks still need filler; strict weather window.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Rust-Oleum+EpoxyShield+Blacktop+Filler+Sealer&tag=sktiger-20)

blocks.h3: Best Heavy-Duty Asphalt Coating: Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000

blocks.p: Black Jack's Drive-Maxx line sits at the premium end of home-center asphalt sealers, and the 1000 is aimed at heavier use. It is an asphalt emulsion with added polymer and filler meant to hold up in tire paths and turning areas where cheaper sealers wear through. Like the Rust-Oleum pick, it restores asphalt to an even black rather than adding color, which is what most blacktop owners mean when they say they want to paint the driveway. Apply it with a squeegee in two thin coats on a clean, dry, crack-filled surface. Each pail costs more and covers less than budget sealers, but premium coats often last longer between applications, which can even out the cost per year. The weather rules match any water-based sealer: warm pavement, mild nights and a dry forecast. Our [asphalt driveway sealer rankings](/best-asphalt-driveway-sealer-reviews/) compare more options.
**Pros:** Premium emulsion with polymer and filler; deep black finish; suited to busy driveways; squeegee application.
**Cons:** Costs more per pail than basic sealers; black only; same strict weather and prep.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Black+Jack+Drive-Maxx+1000+Driveway+Sealer&tag=sktiger-20)

sections.h: Should You Paint, Stain or Seal a Concrete Driveway?

blocks.p: Decide this before you buy anything, because paint is the option with the most upkeep.
A colored film on top. It covers stains, patches and mismatched pours, and it gives the most control over color. It also needs the most prep and can peel if prep or moisture is wrong.

Soaks in or bonds as a thin layer. Penetrating stains do not peel, though they fade and hide stains less well. If the concrete is sound and you mainly want a color refresh, stain is often the safer choice. Our guide to [staining concrete to look like stone](/how-to-stain-concrete-patio-to-look-like-stone/) shows a decorative route.

Protects without changing the color, or adds a wet look depending on the product. For concrete that just needs protection from water, salt and oil, a penetrating sealer is the lowest-upkeep choice; see our [concrete driveway sealer rankings](/best-concrete-driveway-sealer-reviews/).
Sound, evenly colored concrete: consider stain or sealer first. Stained, patched or mismatched concrete you want uniform: paint, if you will do the prep.

sections.h: Can You Paint an Asphalt or Tarmac Driveway?

blocks.p: Not with ordinary paint. Asphalt, called tarmac in the UK, is a flexible, petroleum-based pavement. Concrete and porch paints are rigid and not made for it: they crack as the pavement flexes, and oils in the asphalt can soften or stain them.

blocks.h3: The right refresh is black sealer

blocks.p: A black asphalt sealer or filler sealer restores an even color, hides minor patches and protects the binder. Fill cracks first, clean thoroughly and follow the sealer's weather rules. The two asphalt picks above are good examples, and our [best driveway sealer](/best-driveway-sealer/) guide covers more.

Red, green or tan coatings for asphalt exist, mostly acrylic products used on tennis courts, playgrounds and commercial walkways. They need careful prep and are usually applied by contractors. Concrete and porch paints are not a substitute.
Parking lines on asphalt call for traffic or striping paint, which is made for pavement and dries quickly. Use it sparingly; it can be slippery when wet.

If the asphalt has heavy cracking, raveling or potholes, no coating will make it look new for long. Fix the structure first, and see [sealing asphalt pros and cons](/sealing-asphalt-driveway-pros-and-cons/) and [how to seal a driveway](/how-to-seal-a-driveway/).

blocks.h3: What about Dulux and other UK driveway paints?

blocks.p: Brands sold in the UK and Australia, such as Dulux, make paving and driveway paints that are not generally sold in US home centers. The same rules apply wherever you are: check the label for exterior use and vehicle traffic, and match the product to the surface.

sections.h: What Should You Look For in a Driveway Paint?

blocks.p: The label should list exterior concrete. Sun, rain and freeze-thaw are harder on coatings than a garage interior, and interior-only products may fade, chalk or peel outside.

Tires warm from the road soften paint and lift it when the car pulls away. Products marketed for garage floors and vehicle traffic address this; basic porch paints often do not, which is why they fail first in tire paths.
Painted concrete is smoother than broom-finished concrete and can be slick when wet, especially on slopes. Choose a product that accepts an anti-slip additive.
Labels list coverage per gallon on smooth concrete; rough or porous driveways absorb more. Plan on two coats.

Two-part epoxy is harder, but many garage kits are designed for interior use and can yellow or chalk in direct sun, and some labels exclude exterior use. Check before using any garage product outdoors. For indoor slabs, see our [garage floor epoxy rankings](/best-garage-floor-epoxy/) and [concrete floor paint](/best-concrete-floor-paint/) guide.

Read how the maker says to touch up or recoat in two or three years. One-part acrylic-based paints can usually be scuffed, cleaned and recoated with the same product. A paint that is easy to maintain often beats a harder one that is a chore to refresh, because tire paths will need attention.

sections.h: How Do You Prep a Concrete Driveway So Paint Sticks?

blocks.p: Tape an 18-inch square of clear plastic to the driveway with every edge sealed and leave it 24 hours in the sun. If condensation forms underneath or the concrete darkens, moisture is rising from below, and a film-forming paint is likely to blister or peel. Use a penetrating stain or sealer on that driveway instead.

Sweep, then scrub with a concrete cleaner or degreaser, paying special attention to oil spots. Paint will not stick to oil. Our guides to [removing oil stains from a driveway](/how-to-remove-oil-stains-from-driveway/) and the [best driveway cleaner](/best-driveway-cleaner/) cover the tough spots. A pressure washer helps rinse residue away.

Most floor paints need a slightly rough surface. Use a concrete etcher per the paint maker's directions, or grind for the best bond. A properly etched surface feels like medium-grit sandpaper. If water beads after cleaning, an old sealer is still there and must come off first.
Fill cracks with a flexible concrete sealant and patch chips with a patching compound. Our [driveway crack filler](/best-driveway-crack-filler/) guide covers both.
Allow at least a day or two of dry weather after washing and etching, or longer if the label says so. New concrete typically needs about 28 days of curing before any coating.

sections.h: How Do You Apply Driveway Paint for a Finish That Lasts?

blocks.p: Choose a dry stretch within the label's temperature range, commonly somewhere around 50 to 90 degrees F for both air and surface, with no rain for at least a day. Avoid direct midday sun on very hot days, which can dry the paint too fast and leave lap marks. Mornings and late afternoons often work best.

Cut in edges with a brush, then roll the main area with a 3/8 to 1/2 inch nap roller on an extension pole. Work in sections, keep a wet edge, and apply thin, even coats. Thick coats cure slowly and are more prone to peeling and hot-tire pickup.

Wait the recoat time on the label before the second coat. If you are adding anti-slip grit, most makers recommend mixing it into or broadcasting it onto the final coat; stir often so it stays suspended.

blocks.h3: Typical label guidance for one-part epoxy paint

blocks.p: Many one-part epoxy paints list several days to about a week before parking. Parking early is a leading cause of hot-tire pickup and peeling. Add days in cool or humid weather.

sections.h: Which Driveway Paint Color Still Looks Good in Year Three?

blocks.p: Color decides how long a painted driveway looks fresh more than most buyers expect.

Tires leave dark rubber marks, leaves and pollen leave tan and yellow stains, and road grit settles in low spots. A mid-tone gray, slate or warm tan hides all three. White and very light gray show every mark within weeks; near-black shows dust, salt residue and dried water spots.

Dark coatings absorb more sun, raising the surface temperature on summer afternoons and making softening under warm tires more likely. On south-facing drives and in hot climates, a medium color is safer for durability as well as looks.

Paint a two-foot square in an out-of-the-way corner, let it cure a few days, and look at it in morning and late-afternoon light. Colors look darker and more saturated on a big horizontal surface than on a chip, so many owners go one shade lighter than their first pick.

Keep them simple and away from tire paths. A contrasting border along the edges, a band where the drive meets the sidewalk, or a decorative apron near the garage looks sharp in porch paint while the driving lanes stay one vehicle-rated color.

sections.h: Is Driveway Paint Slippery, and How Do You Fix That?

blocks.p: Painted concrete is noticeably smoother than bare concrete, and water, ice, leaves or an oil film make it slicker still. On a sloped driveway, near steps or on the path to the door, plan for grip from the start.

Fine grit, often polymer beads or silica, mixed into the final coat or broadcast onto it while wet. Many paint brands sell their own. It adds a slight texture that improves grip without feeling rough underfoot. Follow the paint maker's recommendation on type and amount.
Low-luster or satin finishes tend to be less slippery than high gloss, and they hide dirt and tire marks better.
Wear gloves and eye protection when etching, since many etchers are acidic. Keep children and pets off the surface until it cures, and follow the label's safety directions even outdoors.

sections.h: How Long Does Driveway Paint Last?

blocks.p: Lifespan depends on prep, product, climate and traffic more than on the brand.

Any paint on poorly prepped concrete

blocks.p: This guide does not quote product prices, which change by store and season. On a two-car driveway of around 600 square feet, plan on several gallons for two coats, plus cleaner, degreaser, etcher, rollers and possibly anti-slip grit. Asphalt sealers come in roughly five-gallon pails; see [how much it costs to seal a driveway](/how-much-does-it-cost-to-seal-a-driveway/) for the asphalt side.

Keep a quart of leftover paint for touch-ups, wipe up oil drips promptly, and inspect the tire paths each spring. Touching up a small worn patch is easy; repainting a peeling driveway means stripping first.

If the slab is badly cracked, heaving or spalling over large areas, paint will highlight the damage, and the money is better spent on repair. If the concrete is sound and just stained or dull, a weekend of careful prep and two coats is one of the cheapest ways to change the look of the front of a house. For asphalt, follow [how often you should seal your driveway](/how-often-should-you-seal-your-driveway/) instead.

mistakes: Concrete that wicks moisture from below pushes paint off as blisters and peeling, however good the product. Tape down a square of plastic for 24 hours first. If condensation forms underneath, use a penetrating stain or sealer instead of a film-forming paint.

Floor paint needs a slightly rough surface to grip. On smooth or previously sealed concrete it sits on top and peels under tires. Etch or grind as the paint maker directs, rinse well, and make sure water soaks in rather than beading before you paint.
Using porch paint in the tire paths

Porch and patio paints are built for feet. Under car tires, especially warm ones, they scuff, lift and show hot-tire marks quickly. Use a paint rated for vehicle traffic in driving and parking areas and save porch paint for walks and borders.

Concrete and porch paints are rigid and not made for flexible, oily asphalt. They crack and can be softened by oils in the pavement. Refresh blacktop with an asphalt sealer or filler sealer, and leave colored asphalt finishes to specialty coatings.

Many paints feel dry in hours but need several days to a week to cure before cars. Parking early is a leading cause of hot-tire pickup and peeling. Follow the label's vehicle traffic time and add extra days in cool or humid weather.
bottomLine: For a concrete driveway, buy a one-part epoxy-acrylic paint rated for exterior use and vehicle traffic: Behr Premium 1-Part Epoxy for most driveways, KILZ for value, Seal-Krete Epoxy-Seal for low odor, and Behr Porch and Patio only for walks and borders. For asphalt, skip paint and use a black filler sealer such as Rust-Oleum EpoxyShield Blacktop or Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000. Whatever you choose, the moisture test, degreasing, etching and the full cure before parking matter more than the brand on the can.

faqs.q: What is the best paint for a concrete driveway?
faqs.a: A one-part epoxy-acrylic paint rated for exterior concrete and vehicle traffic. Behr Premium 1-Part Epoxy is the best all-round pick, KILZ 1-Part Epoxy Acrylic is the value choice, and Seal-Krete Epoxy-Seal is the low-odor option. Whichever you choose, degrease, etch and moisture-test the concrete first, because prep decides how long it lasts.

faqs.q: What is the hardest wearing driveway paint?
faqs.a: Among DIY roll-on products, one-part epoxy-modified concrete paints marketed for vehicle traffic wear best in tire paths. Professionally installed two-part epoxy or polyaspartic systems are harder still, but many garage epoxy kits are interior-only and can yellow in sun. Check the label for exterior use before using any garage coating on a driveway.

faqs.q: Can you paint an asphalt driveway?
faqs.a: Not with regular paint. Asphalt flexes and contains oils that crack or soften concrete and porch paints. To refresh blacktop, use a black asphalt sealer or filler sealer such as Rust-Oleum EpoxyShield Blacktop or Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000. Colored asphalt coatings exist but are specialty acrylics, mostly contractor-applied on courts and commercial walkways.

faqs.q: How long does driveway paint last?
faqs.a: A well-prepared one-part epoxy paint on concrete commonly lasts a few years before tire paths need touch-ups. Porch paint in tire areas wears faster, and paint on poorly prepared concrete can peel within a season. Black asphalt sealers typically need recoating every two to three years. Keep leftover paint for spot repairs.

faqs.q: Do I need a primer for driveway paint?
faqs.a: Usually not on properly etched bare concrete, because many one-part epoxy floor paints are self-priming there. Some makers recommend a primer for very porous, previously painted or problem surfaces, so check your label. When repainting, the old paint must be sound, cleaned and scuffed, and you should confirm the new product is compatible.

It can be. Painted concrete is smoother than bare concrete and gets slick when wet, especially on slopes. Choose a low-luster finish and add an anti-slip additive to the final coat, mixed in or broadcast onto the wet paint. Pay extra attention near steps, entries and any path people walk regularly.

faqs.q: Can I paint over a sealed concrete driveway?
faqs.a: Only after the old sealer is removed or fully worn off. Paint cannot grip a sealed surface and will peel under tires. Sprinkle water on it: if it beads, sealer is still there. Strip or grind it, then clean and etch. Some clear sealers, such as Seal-Krete Original, state on the label that they can be painted over later.
